quotes.ceb: Proverbs 19:11 – Insightful people restrain their anger; their glory is to ignore an offense.

quotes.niv: Proverbs 21:5 – The plans of the diligent lead to profit as surely as haste leads to poverty.
quotes.esv: Proverbs 21:5 – The plans of the diligent lead surely to abundance, but everyone who is hasty comes only to poverty.
quotes.nkjv: Proverbs 21:5 – The plans of the diligent lead surely to plenty, But those of everyone who is hasty, surely to poverty.
quotes.kjv: Proverbs 21:5 – The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.
quotes.csb: Proverbs 21:5 – The plans of the diligent certainly lead to profit, but anyone who is reckless certainly becomes poor.
quotes.nasb: Proverbs 21:5 – The plans of the diligent certainly lead to advantage, But everyone who is in a hurry certainly comes to poverty.
quotes.ceb: Proverbs 21:5 – The plans of the diligent end up in profit, but those who hurry end up with loss.

quotes.niv: Proverbs 22:29 – Do you see someone skilled in their work? They will serve before kings; they will not serve before officials of low rank.
quotes.esv: Proverbs 22:29 – Do you see a man skillful in his work? He will stand before kings; he will not stand before obscure men.
quotes.nkjv: Proverbs 22:29 – Do you see a man who excels in his work? He will stand before kings; He will not stand before unknown men.
quotes.kjv: Proverbs 22:29 – Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.
quotes.csb: Proverbs 22:29 – Do you see a person skilled in his work? He will stand in the presence of kings. He will not stand in the presence of the unknown.
quotes.nasb: Proverbs 22:29 – Do you see a person skilled in his work? He will stand before kings; He will not stand before obscure people.
quotes.ceb: Proverbs 22:29 – Do you see people who work skillfully? They will work for kings but not for commoners.

quotes.niv: Proverbs 24:3-4 – By wisdom a house is built, and through understanding it is established; through knowledge its rooms are filled with rare and beautiful treasures.
quotes.esv: Proverbs 24:3-4 – By wisdom a house is built, and by understanding it is established; by knowledge the rooms are filled with all precious and pleasant riches.

quotes.csb: Proverbs 24:3-4 – A house is built by wisdom, and it is established by understanding; by knowledge the rooms are filled with every precious and beautiful treasure.
quotes.nasb: Proverbs 24:3-4 – By wisdom a house is built, And by understanding it is established; And by knowledge the rooms are filled With all precious and pleasant riches.
quotes.ceb: Proverbs 24:3-4 – By wisdom a house is built; by understanding it is established. By knowledge rooms are filled with all sorts of precious and pleasant riches.

quotes.niv: Proverbs 25:21-22 – If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat; if he is thirsty, give him water to drink. In doing this, you will heap burning coals on his head, and the Lord will reward you.

quotes.nkjv: Proverbs 25:21-22 – If your enemy is hungry, give him bread to eat; And if he is thirsty, give him water to drink; For so you will heap coals of fire on his head, And the Lord will reward you.
quotes.kjv: Proverbs 25:21-22 – If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord shall reward thee.
quotes.csb: Proverbs 25:21-22 – If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat, and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink, for you will heap burning coals on his head, and the Lord will reward you.
quotes.nasb: Proverbs 25:21-22 – If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat; And if he is thirsty, give him water to drink; For you will heap burning coals on his head, And the Lord will reward you.
quotes.ceb: Proverbs 25:21-22 – If your enemies are starving, feed them some bread; if they are thirsty, give them water to drink. By doing this, you will pile burning coals on their heads, and the Lord will reward you.

quotes.niv: Proverbs 27:1 – Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.
quotes.esv: Proverbs 27:1 – Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.
quotes.nkjv: Proverbs 27:1 – Do not boast about tomorrow, For you do not know what a day may bring forth.
quotes.kjv: Proverbs 27:1 – Boast not thyself of tomorrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.
quotes.csb: Proverbs 27:1 – Don’t boast about tomorrow, for you don’t know what a day might bring.
quotes.nasb: Proverbs 27:1 – Do not boast about tomorrow, For you do not know what a day may bring.
quotes.ceb: Proverbs 27:1 – Don’t brag about tomorrow, for you don’t know what a day will bring.

quotes.niv: Proverbs 28:6 – Better the poor whose walk is blameless than the rich whose ways are perverse.
quotes.esv: Proverbs 28:6 – Better is a poor man who walks in his integrity than a rich man who is crooked in his ways.
quotes.nkjv: Proverbs 28:6 – Better is the poor who walks in his integrity Than one perverse in his ways, though he be rich.
quotes.kjv: Proverbs 28:6 – Better is the poor that walketh in his uprightness, than he that is perverse in his ways, though he be rich.
quotes.csb: Proverbs 28:6 – Better the poor person who lives with integrity than the rich one who distorts right and wrong.
quotes.nasb: Proverbs 28:6 – Better is a poor person who walks in his integrity, Than a person who is crooked, though he is rich.
quotes.ceb: Proverbs 28:6 – Better to be poor and walk in innocence than to be on crooked paths and be rich.

quotes.niv: Proverbs 30:8-9 – Keep falsehood and lies far from me; give me neither poverty nor riches, but give me only my daily bread. Otherwise, I may have too much and disown you and say, ‘Who is the Lord?’ Or I may become poor and steal, and so dishonor the name of my God.
quotes.esv: Proverbs 30:8-9 – Remove far from me falsehood and lying; give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the food that is needful for me, lest I be full and deny you and say, ‘Who is the Lord?’ or lest I be poor and steal and profane the name of my God.
quotes.nkjv: Proverbs 30:8-9 – Remove falsehood and lies far from me; Give me neither poverty nor riches—Feed me with the food allotted to me; Lest I be full and deny You, And say, ‘Who is the Lord?’ Or lest I be poor and steal, And profane the name of my God.
quotes.kjv: Proverbs 30:8-9 – Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.
quotes.csb: Proverbs 30:8-9 – Keep falsehood and deceitful words far from me. Give me neither poverty nor wealth; feed me with the food I need. Otherwise, I might have too much and deny you, saying, ‘Who is the Lord?’ or I might have nothing and steal, profaning the name of my God.
quotes.nasb: Proverbs 30:8-9 – Keep deception and lies far from me, Give me neither poverty nor riches; Feed me with the food that is my portion, So that I will not be full and deny You and say, ‘Who is the Lord?’ And that I will not become impoverished and steal, And profane the name of my God.
quotes.ceb: Proverbs 30:8-9 – Remove falsehood and lies far from me. Don’t give me either poverty or wealth; give me just the food I need. Or I’ll be full and deny you and say, ‘Who is the Lord?’ Or I’ll be poor and steal, and dishonor my God’s name.

quotes.niv: Proverbs 26:20 – Without wood a fire goes out; without a gossip a quarrel dies down.
quotes.esv: Proverbs 26:20 – For lack of wood the fire goes out, and where there is no whisperer, quarreling ceases.
quotes.nkjv: Proverbs 26:20 – Where there is no wood, the fire goes out; And where there is no talebearer, strife ceases.
quotes.kjv: Proverbs 26:20 – Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: so where there is no talebearer, the strife ceaseth.
quotes.csb: Proverbs 26:20 – Without wood, fire goes out; without a gossip, conflict dies down.
quotes.nasb: Proverbs 26:20 – For lack of wood the fire goes out, And where there is no gossiper, quarreling quiets down.
quotes.ceb: Proverbs 26:20 – When there’s no wood, the fire goes out; when there’s no gossiper, arguments stop.

quotes.niv: Proverbs 27:19 – As water reflects the face, so one’s life reflects the heart.
quotes.esv: Proverbs 27:19 – As in water face reflects face, so the heart of man reflects the man.
quotes.nkjv: Proverbs 27:19 – As in water face reflects face, So a man’s heart reveals the man.
quotes.kjv: Proverbs 27:19 – As in water face answereth to face, so the heart of man to man.
quotes.csb: Proverbs 27:19 – As water reflects the face, so the heart reflects the person.
quotes.nasb: Proverbs 27:19 – As in water a face reflects the face, So the heart of a person reflects the person.
quotes.ceb: Proverbs 27:19 – Just as water reflects the face, so the human heart reflects the person.

quotes.nkjv: Proverbs 29:20 – Do you see a man hasty in his words? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
quotes.kjv: Proverbs 29:20 – Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him.
quotes.csb: Proverbs 29:20 – Do you see someone who speaks too soon? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
quotes.nasb: Proverbs 29:20 – Do you see a person who is hasty with his words? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
quotes.ceb: Proverbs 29:20 – Do you see people who are quick to speak? There is more hope for a fool than for them.

quotes.csb: Proverbs 31:26 – She opens her mouth with wisdom and loving instruction is on her tongue.
quotes.nasb: Proverbs 31:26 – She opens her mouth in wisdom, And the teaching of kindness is on her tongue.
quotes.ceb: Proverbs 31:26 – She opens her mouth with wisdom; loving instruction is on her tongue.

quotes.nkjv: Proverbs 10:19 – In the multitude of words sin is not lacking, But he who restrains his lips is wise.
quotes.kjv: Proverbs 10:19 – In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise.
quotes.csb: Proverbs 10:19 – When there are many words, sin is unavoidable, but the one who controls his lips is prudent.
quotes.nasb: Proverbs 10:19 – When there are many words, wrongdoing is unavoidable, But one who restrains his lips is wise.
quotes.ceb: Proverbs 10:19 – Transgression isn’t lacking when it comes to talking too much, but those who restrain their lips are wise.

quotes.esv: Proverbs 13:3 – Whoever guards his mouth preserves his life; he who opens wide his lips comes to ruin.

quotes.kjv: Proverbs 13:3 – He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life: but he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction.
quotes.csb: Proverbs 13:3 – The one who guards his mouth protects his life; the one who opens his lips invites his own ruin.
quotes.nasb: Proverbs 13:3 – One who guards his mouth protects his life; One who opens wide his lips comes to ruin.
quotes.ceb: Proverbs 13:3 – Those who guard their lips guard their lives, but those who talk too much are ruined.

quotes.nasb: Proverbs 14:12 – There is a way which seems right to a person, But its end is the way of death.
